overview.summary: Most public universities in Germany charge no tuition for international students, though you pay a semester contribution and need to show living funds. Many master’s programmes are taught in English; most bachelor’s programmes need German.
overview.educationSystem: Universities (Universitäten) focus on research and theory; universities of applied sciences (Hochschulen / Fachhochschulen) are more practical. Bachelor’s degrees usually take 3–3.5 years and master’s 1.5–2 years.

process: Receive the admission letter (or conditional admission).
Book an online appointment with the German Embassy in Kathmandu.
Prepare academic, language and financial documents.
Attend the appointment, pay the fee and attend any interview.
After approval, provide health insurance and a flight reservation as instructed.
In Germany, register your address and apply for a residence permit.

financialEvidence.requirement: You must prove you can finance your stay. The usual benchmark is €11,904 per year (€992 per month), most often shown through a blocked account (Sperrkonto), a formal declaration of commitment or a scholarship. The German Embassy in Kathmandu says a blocked account is not mandatory when you apply but may be requested during processing.

insurance.requirement: Health insurance is compulsory; students usually join public health insurance after enrolment.

documents: Passport with at least 12 months validity
School leaving and higher secondary certificates, degree transcripts
Financial proof (blocked account, declaration of commitment or scholarship)
Health insurance (after visa approval, per the Kathmandu embassy)

conditions: Up to 140 full days or 280 half days per calendar year.
Student assistant jobs at your university usually do not count towards this limit, but you should inform the foreigners’ office.
Self-employment and freelancing need separate permission.
Many jobs require German. Earnings are not guaranteed and should not be counted on to meet the financial requirement.

postStudyRoutes.name: Residence permit to seek employment
postStudyRoutes.conditions: For graduates of German universities, to look for work that matches the qualification. You can work in any job while searching.

postStudyRoutes.name: EU Blue Card or skilled worker residence permit
postStudyRoutes.conditions: Requires a qualified job offer, with salary thresholds for the Blue Card.

postStudyRoutes.name: Settlement permit
postStudyRoutes.conditions: Possible after a period of qualified work and pension contributions; never automatic.

lifestyle.text: Student residences (Studierendenwerk) are cheapest but have waiting lists. Shared flats (WG) are common. Apply early.
Excellent public transport. Many semester contributions include a regional or Germany-wide ticket.
Four seasons with cold, grey winters.
Health insurance is compulsory; public student insurance covers most treatment.
Generally safe. Registration (Anmeldung) and residence permit deadlines are strict.
